name: Etna summit craters
why: Walk up black ash past lava flows from the 2000s to the edge of Europe's highest active volcano, 3,300 m above the sea you can see.
book: Above Torre del Filosofo (2,920 m) only with an authorised volcano guide; guides save 5 hours with the cable car to 2,500 m and a 4x4 to 2,900 m. The summit is closed by the mayors' ordinances whenever Etna erupts (closed in August 2026): check the day before.
water: Only at Rifugio Sapienza and the cable-car top bar: carry 2-3 litres.
dangers: Volcanic gas and sudden explosions near the craters: follow the guide.
Cold wind and fog at 3,000 m even in August.
Loose ash: heavy going up, ankles on the way down.
turnaround: Turn back where the guide or the ordinance says; without a guide your limit is Torre del Filosofo.

points.name: Crateri Silvestri at Rifugio Sapienza
points.note: 1,910 m: the end of the road, the cable-car station and the Silvestri cones of 1892.

points.name: Etna cable car top (Montagnola)
points.note: 2,500 m, the top of the cable car: black ash slopes; the free walking limit without a guide.

points.name: Torre del Filosofo
points.note: 2,920 m: the 4x4 buses stop here. Above, only with a guide.

points.name: Etna summit craters
points.note: The rim of the summit area near the South-East Crater, about 3,200 m, smoking fumaroles and yellow sulphur.
